sections.h2: Where is Davenport, Iowa, and what is the Quad Cities?
sections.html:
Davenport is the county seat of Scott County and sits on the Mississippi River at the eastern edge of Iowa. It is one of the five Quad Cities, together with Bettendorf in Iowa and Rock Island, Moline and East Moline in Illinois.

The city covers about 66 square miles at an elevation of 660 feet. The river runs east to west here, and the ground slopes up to the north. The 2020 census counted 101,724 residents, which makes Davenport the third most populous city in Iowa after Des Moines and Cedar Rapids. The metro area had 381,801 people.

sections.h2: What is the history of Davenport?
sections.html:
Antoine Le Claire settled Davenport on May 14, 1836, and named it for George Davenport. The city was incorporated on January 25, 1839. The 1832 Black Hawk Purchase, covering about 6 million acres for $640,000, had opened the land to settlement.

The first railroad bridge across the Mississippi opened in 1856 and linked Davenport to Rock Island, Illinois. Abraham Lincoln was the railroad's lead defense lawyer in the litigation that followed a steamboat collision that May. Past industries here included locomotive manufacturing, meatpacking and a Caterpillar loader plant that later closed.

The population has hovered around 100,000 for about four decades, and the 2024 estimate of 100,938 sits right on that line. A flat population means sellers here are not counting on a surge of newcomers, so condition and price carry the sale.

sections.h2: How serious is flooding in Davenport?
sections.html:
Davenport has no permanent flood wall or levee, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi River without one. The older flood wall dates from 1919.

  • The city requires new construction in the floodplain to be elevated or protected by walls.
  • The 1993 Great Flood crested at 22.63 feet on July 9, nearly 8 feet above flood stage.
  • The river flooded again in 2019 and 2023, while higher walls protected downtown Rock Island and Bettendorf in 2019.
  • Credit Island stayed closed for 5.5 months after the 2008 flooding.

Anyone selling a riverside house should expect buyers to ask whether the lot is in a floodplain and whether the house has ever taken water. A cash buyer will ask the same questions but can price the answer in directly.

sections.h2: Which employers drive the Davenport economy?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest employment sector in Davenport, with more than 7,600 jobs. John Deere is the largest single employer in the Quad Cities, with 7,200 workers in the area and 948 at its north Davenport plant.

sections.h2: Which Davenport neighborhoods have a distinct character?
sections.html:
Davenport has several historic districts, and a house inside one may come with expectations about its look and age. Three stand out in the record.

  • Hamburg Historic District: home to the most architecturally significant residences in the old German neighborhoods.
  • Vander Veer Park Historic District: anchored by Vander Veer Park, modeled on New York's Central Park.
  • Village of East Davenport: its Lindsay Park was a Civil War parade ground for Camp McClellan.

The east side has long held higher-end housing. Whatever the area, a seller of an older Davenport house should gather permits, repair receipts and any flood history before talking to buyers.

sections.h2: What school district and colleges serve Davenport?
sections.html:
The Davenport Community School District serves nearly 14,500 students across Davenport, Blue Grass, Buffalo and Walcott and is the fourth largest district in Iowa. It runs four public high schools (Central, West, Mid City and North), six intermediate schools and 23 elementary schools. Assumption is the private high school.

Higher education includes St. Ambrose University, founded in 1882, Palmer College of Chiropractic, Kaplan University and Hamilton Technical College. A house near any of these campuses or schools may draw a different set of buyers than one near the river, so describe the location plainly when you talk to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do roads, bridges and weather affect a Davenport house?
sections.html:
Three bridges link Davenport to Illinois: the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the I-280 Bridge. Interstates 80, 74 and 280 serve the city, along with U.S. 6, 61 and 67 and Iowa 22 and 130. The closest commercial airport is Quad City International in Moline.

The climate is humid continental, with warm humid summers and cold windy winters. Average precipitation is 36.17 inches a year. The record high is 111 degrees on July 12, 1936 and the record low is minus 29 degrees on January 18, 2009. That spread is hard on roofs, siding and older furnaces.

sections.h2: What taxes and filings apply when a Davenport house sells?
sections.html:
The main Iowa cost at recording is the real estate transfer tax. Iowa Code 428A.1 sets it at 80 cents per $500 of value. For a house valued at $200,000, that is $320 (400 units of $500 at 80 cents). The tax does not apply when no consideration is paid.

Property tax is separate. Under Iowa Code 445.37, the first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1. Payments sent online must be entered by midnight on the last day of the month before the delinquent date, with a weekend rule that moves the deadline.

  • Ask the Scott County Treasurer which installments are paid.
  • Have the title company prorate the current bill to the closing date.
  • Confirm the groundwater hazard statement is signed.

sections.h2: What should a Davenport seller gather before talking to buyers?
sections.html:
A short folder of records answers most buyer questions about a Davenport house. The list below follows from the flood and age facts above.

  • Any flood insurance policy, claim or repair receipt, since the Mississippi flooded in 1993, 2008, 2019 and 2023.
  • Elevation or floodplain information for the lot, because new floodplain construction must be raised or walled.
  • Records on wells, tanks or a septic system for the groundwater hazard statement.
  • Lease copies and rent status if tenants live in the house.

If a house needs more repair than you want to fund, say so up front. A cash buyer prices the work, while a conventional buyer's inspection usually turns it into a negotiation.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Davenport house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Davenport skips the listing, the open houses and the lender's timeline. You share the address and the condition of the house, review a written offer, and pick a closing date that suits you.

A title company or attorney then prepares the deed and filings, the buyer pays at closing, and the deed is recorded in Scott County. You can say no to the offer at no cost, and you should compare it with what you would net from a listing after repairs and agent costs.

faqs.q: How many people live in Davenport, Iowa?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 101,724 people in Davenport, and the Census Bureau estimates 100,358 as of July 1, 2025. It is the third most populous city in Iowa.

faqs.q: Does Davenport have a flood wall?
faqs.a: No permanent flood wall or levee protects the city, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi without one. New construction in the floodplain must be elevated or walled.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Davenport home sale?
faqs.a: Iowa charges 80 cents per $500 of value under Iowa Code 428A.1, so a $200,000 value produces $320. No tax applies when there is no consideration.

faqs.q: Who are the largest employers in Davenport?
faqs.a: John Deere is the largest employer in the Quad Cities, with 948 workers at its north Davenport plant. Genesis Health System has 4,900 employees in Davenport, and the school district has 2,237.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1, with a weekend rule that moves the date to the second business day of the month.
